analysis: Reviewed CHANGELOG.md head excerpts (lines 1021-1808) and Makefile (metadata-only unit plus patch). All CHANGELOG content is documentation prose; it makes no executable change. It describes prior or planned security-relevant behavior (SSD prefix cache, T-041; App Attest and attestation changes; payouts; profiler T-051; media egress). I checked it for conflicts with the threat-model assumptions and found no new attack surface. One statement is only loosely consistent with the model: the 'Raise the default shared SSD cache ceiling to 100 GiB, limited to half of available space' entry at ~line 1141. The canonical T-041 says the budget is available-disk/2 with no fixed ceiling. That is a documentation drift in the changelog, and the changelog is not authoritative; it is not a code regression, so I did not report it. The changelog's disclosure of the 'SSD cache enabled by default for Qwen' behavior matches T-041's default-on posture. The Makefile patch (lines 68-87) adds only test targets, three new test commands inside existing `provider-test` and `benchmark-wrapper-test` targets: scripts/test-stage-swiftpm-resource-bundles.py, scripts/benchmarks/test_radix_forward_shapes.py and reports/runtime-kv-path-2026-10-09/qualification/test_curate_runs.py. These run local unit tests and do not touch coordinator authorization, the attestation chain, encryption, billing or payout flows. The referenced test scripts' contents were not supplied, so the Makefile change cannot be fully checked: the scripts could have side effects, but they are repo-local developer tooling and out of the runtime threat-model scope. The Makefile metadata-only unit has no content. Nothing needs follow-up in later passes beyond confirming the new test scripts are hermetic.
